coverage.unit: One contiguous official-source coverage unit with its complete current source text, declared corresponding unified excerpts, and any curated conflict explanation.

coverage.instructions: Assess whether the unofficial unified Ax skill preserves the actionable contract of this official source unit for Ax 25.4.6. Concision, reordering, links to supplied counterpart excerpts, and explicit accurate conflict curation are permitted. Do not demand verbatim prose or obsolete version labels. Judge only supplied evidence; missing counterpart evidence is a gap.

criteria.covered: All consumer-visible requirements, API names and shapes, defaults, constraints, caveats, and meaningful architecture implications in the source are preserved accurately in the supplied unified excerpts.
criteria.organizational: The source unit contains only navigation, repeated framing, or organization whose omission removes no actionable requirement.
criteria.curated: An explicit supplied curation accurately preserves the actionable guidance while explaining a genuine upstream contradiction or implementation limitation.
criteria.mixed: Some actionable source guidance is preserved but at least one contract, constraint, caveat, or relevant design implication is missing or contradicted.
criteria.gap: Actionable source guidance is missing, materially contradicted, or cannot be verified from the supplied counterparts.
criteria.other: The unit cannot be classified because its evidence is malformed or insufficient to identify the source contract.

density.instructions: Assess only substantive unified prose supplied for this coverage unit. Do not penalize necessary contracts or cautions, code samples that teach behavior, explicit curation, or deliberate architecture context.

criteria.sound: The prose is terse yet complete Standard Technical English with no evident meaning loss or avoidable duplication.
criteria.overcompressed: Compression makes an actionable condition, distinction, relationship, or instruction ambiguous or incomplete.
criteria.redundant: Avoidable repeated explanations or filler dilute the instructional content without adding a distinct requirement.
criteria.mixed: Both ambiguity from compression and avoidable redundancy are present.
criteria.not_applicable: No substantive unified prose is supplied for a purely organizational source unit.
criteria.other: The evidence does not support an assessment.

coverage.prefilter: Exclude no declared source coverage units. Deterministically attach exact current source slices and mapped target sections; do not display unflagged bulk units.
coverage.escalation: Read every primary result other than covered/organizational/curated, every density result other than sound/not_applicable, every chosen-label probability below 0.70, every error, and every truncated unit. Confirm or overturn with exact current evidence.

routing.unit: One existing or update-specific user scenario paired with the complete current master skill and the declared owning guide(s).

route.instructions: Given this scenario and the current master skill, decide whether the first reading path preserves the distinction between holistic pre-development architecture and narrow feature implementation. Judge the supplied expected path against the actual wording, not hidden library knowledge.

criteria.correct: The scenario has a clear adequate first path through the master, using Architecture for design or mechanism selection and the owning guide directly for narrow implementation.
criteria.ambiguous: Two materially different first paths remain plausible because master wording lacks a necessary distinction.
criteria.wrong: The declared path conflicts with the master or skips an essential architecture or specialist step.
criteria.other: The scenario or evidence is insufficient to judge the route.

routing.prefilter: Exclude no declared routing scenarios; do not display bulk scenario contents before judging.
routing.escalation: Read every verdict other than correct, every chosen-label probability below 0.70, every error, and every truncated scenario.

architecture.unit: One architecture design scenario with the complete current architecture guide and any directly relevant current specialist excerpts.

adequacy.instructions: Assess whether the supplied unified guidance lets an agent reason about the scenario holistically before implementation, without inventing API contracts or conflating execution, state, transport, provider, evaluation, or trust boundaries. Do not require architecture prose for purely local implementation details.

criteria.sufficient: The supplied guidance contains the relevant design distinctions, tradeoffs, lifecycle or quality constraints, and route to the implementation contract.
criteria.mixed: The guidance supports part of the design but omits or blurs at least one material boundary or tradeoff.
criteria.gap: The guidance lacks a material design consideration required by the scenario or gives a materially wrong one.
criteria.not_applicable: The scenario is solely a local implementation detail with no relevant architecture decision.
criteria.other: The scenario or evidence is insufficient to judge adequacy.

architecture.prefilter: Exclude no declared architecture scenarios; do not display bulk scenario contents before judging.
architecture.escalation: Read every verdict other than sufficient/not_applicable, every chosen-label probability below 0.70, every error, and every truncated scenario.
